newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ICE rates Graboplast shares as 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: ICE rates Graboplast shares as 'buy'.

text.p: Hungarian home improvement product maker Graboplast could see above-inflation earnings growth in 1997 and 1998, London-based ICE Securities said, rating the shares a buy.

"Graboplast proved to be one of the best performing mid-capitalised stocks on the Hungarian market and the success story is set to continue," ICE's analyst Rudi Voros said in a market research report dated January 28.

"While we forecast 35 percent earnings per share (EPS) growth for 1997, followed by 28 percent in 1998, given the company's aggressive acquisition strategy, earnings could leapfrog even further in the next few years," he said.
These EPS forecasts are above the Hungarian government's inflation target of around 17 percent for 1997.
Graboplast has a solid base for significant further progress with its acquisition policy which comes in addition to its existing market niches, Voros said.
Recent acquisitions include the purchase of Sotex carpet factory and Uniontext textile company in 1995, and Keszta-Dunawall wallpaper firm in 1996.
"Graboplast's main strength lies in a motivated, focused management, and in a strategy which drives earnings ahead at a considerable pace," Voros added.
"We believe that the company is one of the most likely candidates for long-term outperformance and as such, should be part of any emerging European market portfolio."
